newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia sees 1997 cement demand at 17.4 mln tns.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia sees 1997 cement demand at 17.4 mln tns.

text.p: Cement demand in Malaysia is expected to rise to 17.4 million tonnes this year from an estimated 14.8 million tonnes in 1996, Domestic Trade and Consumer Affairs Minister Abu Hassan Omar said on Thursday.
Local cement demand will remain strong based on forecasts that the construction sector will grow by an annual 10.2 percent under the Seventh Malaysia Plan (1996-2000), he said.

Speaking at a signing ceremony involving a cement plant project, Abu Hassan said there was still cement shortage in the country as domestic manufacturing capacity stood at 11.32 million tonnes in 1995. He did not give figures for 1996.
Last year, the government had to import the shortfall from more than six countries.

"Based on the 18 to 20 percent annual increase in demand and expansion programmes together with the building of new plants, local cement output is expected to meet internal demand only from 1998," he said.
